title: Human Gestures Are Efficient
text:
Code for dataset loading, plotting defaults







We load the gesture dataframe.


Code
library(cowplot)
library(ggplot2)
# Use this conditional approach:
if (rstudioapi::isAvailable()) {
  # Running in RStudio
  current_dir <- dirname(rstudioapi::getSourceEditorContext()$path)
} else {
  # Running outside RStudio (like command line quarto)
  current_dir <- here::here()
}

# load full data
fulldat <- read.csv(paste0(current_dir, "/Data_Output/gestures_long.csv"))
fulldat$gesture_id <- as.factor(fulldat$gesture_id)
fulldat$corpus <- as.factor(fulldat$corpus)
fulldat$speaker <- as.factor(fulldat$speaker)
fulldat$subtype <- as.factor(fulldat$subtype)
fulldat$condition <- as.factor(fulldat$condition)

# gesture category only
gesdat <- subset(fulldat, condition == "gesture")
gesdat$corpus <- droplevels(gesdat$corpus)
gesdat$speaker <- droplevels(gesdat$speaker)
gesdat$gesture_id <- droplevels(gesdat$gesture_id)

# objman category only
objman_dat <- subset(fulldat, condition == "objman")
objman_dat$corpus <- droplevels(objman_dat$corpus)
objman_dat$speaker <- droplevels(objman_dat$speaker)
objman_dat$gesture_id <- droplevels(objman_dat$gesture_id)







Code
# Set some plotting defaults
library(RColorBrewer)

# Enhanced plotting theme
my_theme <- function() {
  theme_cowplot() +
  theme(
    text = element_text(size = 10, family = "sans"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 9, color = "grey20"),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", hjust = 0),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "grey80"),
    legend.key = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)
  )
}

# colors - more contrastive
corpus_colors <- c(
  "ECOLANG" = "#E41A1C",
  "GESres" = "#377EB8", 
  "MULTISIMO" = "#4DAF4A",
  "SAGA" = "#984EA3",
  "SAGAplus" = "#FF7F00",
  "ZHUBO" = "#F781BF"
)








The models that we construct all share that they have as their response variable the log-transformed subm_dur_ms (submovement duration), and as a fixed effect predictor the log-transformed n_submovements (number of submovements). Since there are multiple observations of submovement durations per gesture, we include gesture_id as a random effect nested within speaker and corpus to account for this non-independence. We follow closely the modeling approach of (Wascher and Youngblood 2025) as provided here https://masonyoungblood.github.io/crow_efficiency/.
Below the blocks allows for inspection of the mixed regression models, their equations, plotting code.






Key mixed regression models for assessing Menzerath-Altman law







Code
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(dplyr)
library(equatiomatic)

# remove any rows with single submovement gestures
gesdat <- gesdat[gesdat$n_submovements > 1, ]

# Basic Menzerath model with corpus in random structure
gesture_menz_model <- lmer(scale(log(subm_dur_ms)) ~ scale(log(n_submovements)) + (1|corpus/speaker/gesture_id), data = gesdat)

# For LaTeX output
equationmenz <- extract_eq(gesture_menz_model, use_coefs = TRUE)











Equations of the models





\[
\begin{aligned}
  \operatorname{\widehat{subm\_dur\_ms}}_{i}  &\sim N \left(0_{\alpha_{j[i],k[i],l[i]}} - 0.08_{\beta_{1}}(\operatorname{scale(\log(n\_submovements))}), \sigma^2 \right) \\
    \alpha_{j}  &\sim N \left(0, 0.17 \right)
    \text{, for gesture\_id:(speaker:corpus) j = 1,} \dots \text{,J} \\
    \alpha_{k}  &\sim N \left(0, 0.12 \right)
    \text{, for speaker:corpus k = 1,} \dots \text{,K} \\
    \alpha_{l}  &\sim N \left(0, 0.12 \right)
    \text{, for corpus l = 1,} \dots \text{,L}
\end{aligned}
\]









Plotting code for Menzerath’s law models







Code
library(ggplot2)
library(cowplot)
library(lmerTest)
library(svglite)

# create plots folder
dir.create(paste0(current_dir, "/plots"), showWarnings = FALSE)

# Extract fixed effects coefficients
coef_menz <- fixef(gesture_menz_model)

# get median submovement duration per gesture
gesdat_summary <- gesdat %>%
  group_by(gesture_id, n_submovements, corpus) %>%
  summarise(subm_dur_median = median(subm_dur_ms), .groups = "drop")

# scale using the full dataset parameters (as.numeric to avoid matrix)
gesdat_summary$x_scaled <- as.numeric(scale(log(gesdat_summary$n_submovements)))
gesdat_summary$y_scaled <- as.numeric(scale(log(gesdat_summary$subm_dur_median)))

# Create prediction line using same scaling
pred_x <- seq(min(gesdat_summary$x_scaled), max(gesdat_summary$x_scaled), length.out = 100)
pred_y <- coef_menz[1] + coef_menz[2] * pred_x
pred_line <- data.frame(x = pred_x, y = pred_y)

# per-corpus regression lines
corpus_lines <- gesdat_summary %>%
  group_by(corpus) %>%
  summarise(
    intercept = coef(lm(y_scaled ~ x_scaled))[1],
    slope = coef(lm(y_scaled ~ x_scaled))[2],
    x_min = min(x_scaled),
    x_max = max(x_scaled),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  do({
    x_seq <- seq(.$x_min, .$x_max, length.out = 50)
    data.frame(corpus = .$corpus, x = x_seq, y = .$intercept + .$slope * x_seq)
  })

# main plot with all data
p1 <- ggplot(gesdat_summary, aes(x = x_scaled, y = y_scaled, color = corpus)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 2) +
  geom_line(data = corpus_lines, aes(x = x, y = y, color = corpus), linewidth = 0.8, alpha = 2) +
  geom_line(data = pred_line, aes(x = x, y = y), color = "black", linewidth = 1.2, inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 2) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, 
           label = sprintf("overall: y = %.3f + %.3fx", coef_menz[1], coef_menz[2]),
           hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.5, size = 2.5) +
  labs(x = "Scaled log(Number of Submovements)", 
       y = "Scaled log(Submovement Duration)",
       title = "Menzerath's Law: All Corpora") +
  scale_color_manual(values = corpus_colors) +
  my_theme()


Warning: Using `size` aesthetic for lines was deprecated in ggplot2 3.4.0.
ℹ Please use `linewidth` instead.


Code
# faceted plot per corpus
p_facet <- ggplot(gesdat_summary, aes(x = x_scaled, y = y_scaled, color = corpus)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 2) +
  geom_line(data = corpus_lines, aes(x = x, y = y, color = corpus), linewidth = 2) +
  geom_line(data = pred_line, aes(x = x, y = y), color = "black", linewidth = 1, linetype = "dashed", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ corpus, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Scaled log(Number of Submovements)", 
       y = "Scaled log(Submovement Duration)",
       title = "Menzerath's Law: Per Corpus") +
  scale_color_manual(values = corpus_colors, guide = "none") +
  my_theme() +
  theme(strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey90"),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"))

# combined plot
p_combined <- plot_grid(p1, p_facet, ncol = 1, rel_widths = c(1, 1.5), labels = c("A", "B"))

# save plots
ggsave(paste0(current_dir, "/plots/menzerath_all_corpora.svg"), p1, width = 8, height = 6)
ggsave(paste0(current_dir, "/plots/menzerath_per_corpus.svg"), p_facet, width = 12, height = 8)
ggsave(paste0(current_dir, "/plots/menzerath_combined.svg"), p_combined, width = 16, height = 6)

Confound analysis: Object manipulation category






Object manipulation per-corpus model fitting







Code
# fit for objman - only ECOLANG has data
corpus_results_objman <- fit_corpus_model(objman_dat, "ECOLANG")

corpus_table_objman <- corpus_results_objman
corpus_table_objman$beta_fmt <- sprintf("%.3f", corpus_table_objman$beta)
corpus_table_objman$SE_fmt <- sprintf("%.3f", corpus_table_objman$SE)
corpus_table_objman$CI_fmt <- sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", corpus_table_objman$CI_low, corpus_table_objman$CI_high)
corpus_table_objman$p_fmt <- ifelse(corpus_table_objman$p < 0.001, "< 0.001", sprintf("%.3f", corpus_table_objman$p))
corpus_table_objman$Speaker_SD_fmt <- sprintf("%.3f", corpus_table_objman$Speaker_SD)
corpus_table_objman$R2_fixed_fmt <- sprintf("%.3f", corpus_table_objman$R2_fixed)
corpus_table_objman$R2_total_fmt <- sprintf("%.3f", corpus_table_objman$R2_total)
corpus_table_objman$delta_AIC_fmt <- sprintf("%.1f", corpus_table_objman$delta_AIC)
